input.brief: Write a long-form guide for homeowners who want to switch their home to renewable energy, step by step.

output.title: Switching your home to renewable energy, step by step
output.subtitle: A clear path for homeowners, from reading the bill to switching the lights on.

intro.hook: Begin with a homeowner reading an energy bill and wondering what a realistic first move would be, then promise an order of steps that avoids expensive mistakes.

sections.heading: Understand what your home uses today
sections.angle: Teach the reader to read their bills and find where energy goes, because every later decision depends on knowing the baseline.

visuals.prompt: A homeowner's kitchen table with a printed utility bill, a calculator and a pen in warm daylight, no people visible
visuals.alt: A utility bill and a calculator on a kitchen table
visuals.caption: Everything starts with knowing what the house uses

sections.heading: Cut waste before you generate anything
sections.angle: Argue that efficiency work is the cheapest source of energy, and compare the usual measures by effort and payoff.

sections.heading: Choose the right way to generate
sections.angle: Explain the main options for a home, such as rooftop solar, a heat pump and buying green power, and how to decide between them for a given house.

visuals.prompt: A modern house with solar panels on a pitched roof under a clear sky, photographed from the street
visuals.alt: A house with solar panels on its roof
visuals.caption: Rooftop generation is one option among several

sections.heading: Work out the cost and how you will pay
sections.angle: Set out the main ways to finance the switch and the questions to ask installers, so the reader can compare offers on equal terms.

visuals.title: Ways to pay for the switch

sections.heading: Choose an installer you can trust
sections.angle: Give the reader a practical way to vet installers: credentials, references, written quotes and what a good site visit looks like.

visuals.prompt: A friendly technician in work clothes and a hard hat checking a clipboard beside an outdoor heat pump unit
visuals.alt: A technician checking a clipboard beside an outdoor heat pump
visuals.caption: A good installer explains the plan before touching anything

sections.heading: Switch on, then keep measuring
sections.angle: Describe what to check after installation and how to track the results against the original baseline so the reader knows the switch worked.

visuals.prompt: A wall-mounted smart energy display in a hallway showing a simple glowing ring graphic, soft indoor light
visuals.alt: A wall-mounted energy display showing a glowing ring
visuals.caption: Keep measuring against the baseline

conclusion.heading: Take the first step this month
